{{Quote|Try to ''understand'', Skywalker&hellip;You made it ''off'' this sandpile. But Camie an' me are ''stuck'' here&hellip;We've got to get by as ''best'' we can!|Laze "Fixer" Loneozner, to Luke Skywalker|<ref name="sw31">[[Star Wars (1977) 31|''Star Wars'' (1977) 31]]</ref>}}
'''Laze Loneozner''', better known as '''Fixer''', was a skilled mechanic and one of [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker's]] childhood friends from [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]]. He was the husband of [[Camie Loneozner|Camie]].

==Biography==
===Childhood===
{{Quote|Wanna know what Fixer and Tank called us?''"<br />"''Huh?''"<br />"''They called us small fry. Can you believe that?"|Windy Starkiller and Luke Skywalker|<ref name="lifeofluke">''[[A New Hope: The Life of Luke Skywalker]]''</ref>}}
The [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] Laze "Fixer" Loneozner grew up on the desolate world of [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]]. He often passed time with his friends Luke, [[Biggs Darklighter/Legends|Biggs]], [[Windy Starkiller|Windy]], [[Deacon|Deak]], and especially his girlfriend [[Camie Loneozner|Camie]].

In [[6 BBY/Legends|6 BBY]], Loneozner and [[Janek Sunber/Legends|Janek Sunber]] were old enough to drive landspeeders, and they raced in the canyon south of [[Ja-Mero Ridge/Legends|Ja-Mero Ridge]]. They flouted at Windy Starkiller and Luke Skywalker, who at that time were not old enough to join them.<ref name="lifeofluke" />

When Fixer had to take the qualifying test for the Imperial Academy, he walked in, filled out his name, and walked out.<ref name="radio">{{SWRadio|A Wind to Shake the Stars}}</ref>

===King of the sandsurfers===
{{Quote|That guy's crazy, but boy can he surf!|Biggs Darklighter|<ref name="Trilogy SB">''[[The Movie Trilogy Sourcebook]]''</ref>}}
[[File:LazeLoneozner.jpg|thumb|left|225px|Fixer working at Tosche Station.]]
At one point, Fixer got tired of always being beaten at Skyhopper racing and womp-rat hunting by Skywalker and Darklighter, so he created something at which he could be the best: his own sport, "[[sandsurfing]]." In the sport, a person would wear repulsor disks on their feet and grab on to a set of handles that connected to a sand skiff by a thin cord. As the skiff moved along, the "surfer" would perform all manners of flips and tricks on the countless sloping dunes and unobstructed sand of the Dune Sea. But as it turned out, Darklighter and Skywalker were also quite good at sandsurfing. When Darklighter did three double-flips in a row, even Camie was impressed, and she hung on his arm when they returned to [[Tosche Station/Legends|Tosche Station]] later to celebrate. This pushed Fixer over the edge. The next morning they all went out to the [[Dune Sea/Legends|Dune Sea]] where Fixer claimed he would attempt the "greatest stunt of all time." He had programmed a skiff's [[Autopilot/Legends|autopilot]] to drive itself.

His run started out well, with him performing loops, a half-moon, and even a double backwards loop (which no one had ever done before). After all that, his friends thought he was done, so they went to congratulate him. But then the skiff sped up and took a sharp turn, heading itself for the [[Great Pit of Carkoon/Legends|Great Pit of Carkoon]]. Unable to stop him, all his friends could do was watch. Fixer had planned the whole thing and had already prepared ramps of sand on both sides of the pit. While he hit the first ramp perfectly, he fell a half meter short of the landing and he hit the side of the pit, engulfed in an explosion of sand. Camie, tears streaming down her face, would have dived in after him had Skywalker not stopped her. Darklighter flew his skiff over to the unconscious Fixer, who was slowly sliding down to the mouth of the [[Sarlacc/Legends|sarlacc]]. The situation got even worse when the sarlacc started probing the sand with one of its tentacles. Darklighter tied a cord around his waist and jumped down into the pit, being careful not to shift the sand and cause Fixer to slide even faster. Just as Darklighter reached him, the sarlacc's tentacle wrapped around Fixer's chest. Darklighter whipped out his [[Vibroblade/Legends|vibroblade]], but as he went after the tentacle, more and more tentacles went after ''him''. Then Skywalker grabbed his punch gun and, despite the bad angle and long range, shot the tentacle that was holding his friend. Luke then took off in the skiff, pulling both his friends to safety.

Fixer suffered only a minor concussion and a broken nose&mdash;the first from the crash, the latter from Camie after he healed from the concussion. Though he was fully recovered in two weeks, he spent the next month at home, grounded for being so reckless. Biggs and Luke had no problem admitting that Fixer was indeed the king of the sandsurfers and that they couldn't duplicate his stunt, but that just didn't make Fixer feel quite as good as he'd thought it would.

Not much before Darklighter was about to leave Tatooine for the Imperial Academy, Owen Lars's [[WED-15 Treadwell droid/Legends|Treadwell]], [[WED-15-77/Legends|WED-15-77]] broke down. Skywalker took parts of the droid to Fixer, but he had a weeks backlog on the Tosche Station, so he couldn't begin working on the Treadwell,<ref name="sw17">[[Star Wars (1977) 17|''Star Wars'' (1977) 17]]</ref> but eventually the droid got repaired.<ref name="novel" />

===The war comes to Tatooine===
{{Quote|Fixer and I don't have much time for ''politics''&hellip;we're kept busy just trying to make our ''lives'' a little bit better!|Camie Loneozner, to Luke Skywalker|<ref name="sw31" />}}
[[File:Fixer_marvel.jpg|thumb|right|215px|Luke and Fixer reunited.]]
Fixer had a job at Tosche Station in [[Anchorhead/Legends|Anchorhead]]. Since the owner, [[Merl Tosche/Legends|Merl Tosche]], was rarely around, and neither were many customers, Fixer pretty much ran the place himself. He and his friends usually worked on their [[Skyhopper/Legends|skyhoppers]] or [[Landspeeder/Legends|landspeeders]] there. Fixer had a [[Fixer's landspeeder/Legends|five-engined landspeeder]], and he was also secretly rebuilding a [[Podracer/Legends|podracer]] that he planned to sell for a very high price in [[Mos Espa/Legends|Mos Espa]] in order to have enough money to throw a huge wedding for him and Camie.

At one point, not much before Darklighters' return, Fixer and his friend gathered in [[Beggar's Canyon/Legends|Beggar's Canyon]]. By the time Skywalker and Windy arrived on the former skyhopper, Fixer, Camie, and Deak were already there, enjoying [[malt]] juices. Fixer had a race with Skywalker down [[Beggar's Canyon/Legends|Beggar's Canyon]] in their skyhoppers. During the speed run, Deak rode with Fixer and Windy accompanied Skywalker. Fixer figured his route through the [[Bottleneck (Tatooine)|Bottleneck]], which he thought to be the perfect route, which would earn him new record time around Beggar's Canyon. However, Skywalker took a dangerous maneuver: he flew through the [[Stone Needle/Legends|Stone Needle]], lost a stabilizer, but eventually beat Fixer.<ref name="radio" />

Immediately afterwards, he engaged in a non-lethal dogfight, which he also lost, much to his dismay.

The day Biggs Darklighter returned home from his training at the [[Imperial Academy/Legends|Imperial Academy]] and went to Tosche Station, Fixer and Camie were lounging around when Luke Skywalker, whom they more often referred to as "Wormie," walked in to tell everyone about the [[Battle of Tatooine (Galactic Civil War)|space battle]] he had just seen. The four of them walked outside to check it out, but while the other three all looked through a pair of [[Electrobinoculars/Legends|electrobinoculars]], Fixer wasn't interested enough to look, and instead kept his attention on Camie. As they went back inside, he told Luke that he doubted if the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] would even fight to save the [[Tatoo system/Legends|Tatoo system]]. Not much later, Fixer joined his droids in performing repairs in the station's repair bay.<ref name="novel" />

The next day, Imperial stormtroopers hit on the Lars homestead and killed Owen and Beru Lars, and this way they forced Luke Skywalker to join [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] in his quest for the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebellion]]. Everyone, including Fixer thought that the Tusken Raiders hit the homestead and Skywalker died along with his relatives. Sometime later, after the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]], Fixer and Camie got married. Fixer quit his job at Tosche Station when the [[House of Tagge/Legends|House of Tagge]] came to Tatooine and brought up a lot of [[Moisture farm/Legends|moisture farms]]. The Tagge outfit set him and Camie up at the Darklighters' old home and made Fixer a caretaker for their new properties, one of which was the old [[Lars homestead/Legends|Lars homestead]]. Fixer was at the Lars house one day when he caught Skywalker, who he thought to be a thieving scavenger snooping around. He pulled a [[Blaster/Legends|blaster]] on Skywalker, but when he had him toss his own blaster, Skywalker spun around and destroyed Fixer's gun with [[Anakin Skywalker's second lightsaber/Legends|his lightsaber]]. Recognizing his old friend, Fixer told Skywalker about his new business, but when Imperials showed up, Skywalker fled with his droids. Fixer and Camie felt they had to do whatever he could to protect their job. Since they suspected Skywalker of being a Rebel, they sold him out to the Empire. However, Fixer searched for Skywalker and caught up with him in [[Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina/Legends|Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina]] in [[Mos Eisley/Legends|Mos Eisley]] to warn him of their treachery.<ref name="sw31" />

At one point during the time of the rebellion, Fixer was serving ale at Tosche Station when the worst sandstorm in a decade hit Anchorhead and a group of Rebels, local citizens, and stormtroopers took shelter inside. After the troopers arrived, a firefight broke out.<ref name="Night">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/sw20010621a2|text=A Night at Tosche Station|int=A Night at Tosche Station}}</ref>

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|Listen, anything the great Biggs Darklighter could do, ''I'' can do!|Fixer, to Camie|<ref name="radio" />}}
Fixer tended to be highly defensive of Camie. While they were watching the battle above Tatooine, Fixer gave Skywalker a hard look when the latter complained about Camie's lack of care when she grabbed his binoculars away.<ref name="novel" /> However, he didn't care for her opinion when it came to her admiration of Darklighter.<ref name="radio" /> His opinion of Skywalker was much lower, he gave the boy derogatory nicknames such as small fry or Wormie.<ref name="lifeofluke" /><ref name="radio" />

He was good at repairing droids, which Skywalker knew, leading him to once bring a broken [[WED Treadwell repair droid/Legends|Treadwell]] to him for repair.<ref name="sw17" /> However, he could occasionally act immaturely, in Camie's opinion, in that he'd sometimes steal parts for his repairs to his [[Skyhopper/Legends|Skyhopper]].<ref name="radio" />

Fixer envied Darklighter's piloting skill, and was eager to match his records. However, he wasn't so keen on entering the Imperial Academy due to his preference for being his own boss. He even went so far as to sabotage his qualifying test to enter the academy.<ref name="radio" /> He also didn't care about the possible political repercussions of such a move against the Empire, or politics in general.<ref name="sw31" />

Darklighter found Fixer smart enough to know that the man was better off being the big noise in a small room than to hide in the background.<ref name="radio" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|Fixer was described to me as a grease-monkey guy, who worked on fixing droids and other stuff. A mechanic. He was also very protective of his girlfriend Camie Marstrap, and very dismissive of Luke, who he called 'Wormy.' Despite our character's on-screen relationship, Mark Hamill and I got along well.|Anthony Forrest|<ref name="Let Me See">{{InsiderCite|216|Let Me See Your Identification}}</ref>}}
[[File:Camie-Biggs-Fixer-skretch.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Sketch of Camie Loneozner, Darklighter and Fixer]]
The Fixer character first appeared in the [[December]] [[1976]] [[Star Wars: A New Hope (novelization)|novelization]] of [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']],<ref name="novel" /> ghostwritten by [[Alan Dean Foster]].<ref name="ANH novel SE">[[Star Wars: A New Hope (novelization)|''Star Wars Episode IV: A New Hope'' novelization]], [[The Star Wars Trilogy Special Edition|Special Edition]] foreword by [[George Lucas]]</ref> His first visual appearance occurred in [[1977]] in [[Marvel Comics]]'s [[Star Wars (1977) 1|adaptation]] of ''A New Hope''.<ref name="marvel">[[Star Wars (1977) 1|''Star Wars'' (1977) 1]]</ref> Fixer's scene was cut before the release of the film. In [[1979]], [[Ballantine Books]] published [[The Art of Star Wars Episode IV: A New Hope|''The Art of Star Wars'']], which featured the full script of the film and many production sketched, including one by [[Wikipedia:Costume designer|costume designer]] [[John Mollo]] that depicted Fixer. Although the caption of image identified "Camie, The Fixer and Biggs", they seemed to be Camie, Biggs and Fixer per their clothes.<ref name="artof">''[[The Art of Star Wars Episode IV: A New Hope]]''</ref>

The Anchorhead scene from [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''A New Hope'']] has been portrayed more or less the same in every adaptation over the years. However, the creators of the comic [[Star Wars: Empire: Darklighter|''Darklighter'']] decided to change the previously established events. In the comic, when Biggs Darklighter returned to Tosche Station, Camie joyfully greeted him with a kiss on the cheek. But she was getting too close for Fixer, and he told her to cut it out and quickly jumped out of his seat, pushed his girlfriend out of the way, and grabbed Biggs' jacket. He was ready to let loose on him when Luke walked in to report the space battle he had just seen. It is not known if this change is canon.

In the scenes deleted from ''A New Hope'', Fixer was played by [[Anthony Forrest]]. He was played by [[Adam Arkin]] in the [[Star Wars (radio)|radio drama]]. [[Timothy Omundson]] provided his voice for a scene in ''[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron III: Rebel Strike]]''. In the video game, the player races and wins a dogfight against Fixer during the training mission.

Fixer's real name was not revealed until ''[[Inside the Worlds of Star Wars Trilogy]]''.

The word ''laze'' can mean "to lounge" or "to pass time lazily." The character's name could have easily been inspired by this, given his lethargy in the scene deleted from ''A New Hope''. Laze is also homonymous with the word "lase", which means to emit coherent radiation by the action of a laser.

[[RC-1140/Legends|Delta 40]] in ''[[Star Wars: Republic Commando]]'' is also named "Fixer," a reference to this character.<ref name="Blog-RyanKaufman|8">{{Blog|RyanKaufman|8|What's In a Name?}}</ref>
